newsitem.title: USA: ComEd sees 1,040 MW Ill. nuke back mid-Sept.
newsitem.headline: ComEd sees 1,040 MW Ill. nuke back mid-Sept.

text.p: Commonwealth Edison Co's (ComEd) 1,040 MW Zion nuclear power unit 1 in Zion, Ill. was expected to restart near mid-September, the company said Tuesday.
"It looks like about the middle of the month (for the Zion 1 restart)," company spokesman Gary Wald said.
The unit was shut August 27 for repairs to a motor operating valve on the pressurizing system.

Also, ComEd's Dresden unit 2 nuclear power station at Morris, Ill. was expected to boost output to 60 percent of capacity Tuesday and hold at that level for several days during feedwater testing, Wald said.
The 794 MW unit was shut May 26 for repairs.
Commonwealth Edision is a subsidiary of Unicom Corp.
